{"blockedBy":{"nodes":[],"totalCount":0},"body":"## Parent

#1186

## What to build

Pilot, the lane's tracer bullet. An implementer in a kit lane runs `just fast` while another lane's full gate holds the box's one heavy-run slot, and its own lane holds no grant: the run starts at once, takes no slot, runs on the fast tier's small fixed worker count, says so, and passes. The full gate (`just check`) still asks the slot by the old rule and runs at full width. How the gate tells a fast-tier run (quality #recipes-static-first, as amended): by what the run holds, only static checks and integration tests (no item carrying the e2e kind), on no more workers than the cap; a run holding any end-to-end test, or more workers than the cap, asks the slot as before, so a full run cannot pass itself off as fast and no caller flag or env var dodges it. The decision lives in the gate's slot plugin and runner (tests/gate/heavy_slot.py, the gate's runner), not in the slot queue module; the cap is a key in the kit's gate-budget.toml beside heavy_items, its number picked from measurement: a one-script and a worst-case (shared-machinery) fast run alone, and the same two while a full gate runs beside them, with the full gate's wall time with and without them. octo-feather-slot --help's statement of the heavy rule points at the exemption. Templates unchanged (their gate has no slot); the qc and qa sandboxes and CI unchanged (no slot there).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] quality#acceptance-fast-slot-free: with another lane holding the heavy grant and its lock, a lane with no grant runs `just fast`; it starts at once, prints that it runs as the fast tier on the capped worker count, takes no slot and passes; `just check` in the same lane is still refused for want of a grant
- [ ] demo: `just fast` in the lane worktree while another lane's full gate holds the heavy slot: starts at once, names the fast tier and its worker count, passes

## Seams

Seam: quality#acceptance-fast-slot-free: `just fast`

## Skills

Skills: tdd, python
